newsitem.title: UK: West Bromwich Albion sacks manager Buckley.
newsitem.headline: West Bromwich Albion sacks manager Buckley.

text.p: English first division soccer club West Bromwich Albion said on Wednesday it had sacked manager Alan Buckley following a meeting with chairman Tony Hale.

The club, which is listed on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) as West Bromwich Albion Plc, said Buckley "had worked very hard for the club" but that it would be looking to employ a high profile manager "with a proven record of success".
West Bromwich, based in the West Midlands, said in a statement that Buckley's assistant Arthur Mann would serve as caretaker manager with the assistance of club coach John Trewick.
The club said it was seeking a new manager who would "be capable of taking the club into the premier league".
West Bromwich is currently languishing in 17th position in the 24-team first division, with only seven wins in 28 matches.
